task.title: VISIBILITY
task.spec:
You are working in a checkout of shopizer, a Java e-commerce platform (Maven, several modules; JDK 21 is installed and JAVA_HOME is set).

Merchants hide products they are still preparing, or have paused, by sending "visible": false. It doesn't work. The flag is used as "available" instead, a hidden product still opens for anyone and still appears in the product lists, and every product reads back as visible. A product created with "available": false comes back available.

Make visibility and availability work, separately:

- Creating a product (POST /api/v1/private/product) or replacing it (PUT /api/v1/private/product/{id}) stores "visible" and "available" as sent, independently of each other.
- For shoppers, a hidden product doesn't exist: GET /api/v2/product/{sku} and GET /api/v2/product/name/{friendlyUrl} give HTTP 404 Not Found, GET /api/v1/products and GET /api/v2/products don't list it, and it can't be added to a cart (HTTP 404). A cart that already holds it when it is hidden can't be checked out (POST /api/v1/cart/{code}/checkout gives HTTP 409 Conflict, and no order is created) until the product is removed from the cart or shown again.
- Merchants still see their hidden products: GET /api/v1/private/products (protected like the other /api/v1/private endpoints) lists all of the store's products, hidden or not, with the same query parameters and response as GET /api/v1/products, each product showing its "visible" flag.
- A visible product shows "visible": true, and "available" as stored. A visible product that is not available is shown with "available": false and can't be added to a cart.
- GET /api/v2/product/name/{friendlyUrl} returns the same product as GET /api/v2/product/{sku}.
- Showing a hidden product again (replacing it with "visible": true) brings it back everywhere, with its stock and price unchanged. Orders that include a product that was hidden later are unaffected.

When you have finished, reply with one short paragraph saying what you changed.

findings.problem: Required end-to-end verification for independent visibility/availability persistence, shopper 404/list filtering, private merchant listing, cart rejection, checkout HTTP 409/no-order behavior, re-showing, and order preservation was not run or supplied. GitHub reports zero check runs.
findings.impact: The implementation may compile while still failing one or more task-level API behaviors; the acceptance criteria cannot be confirmed from the available evidence.
findings.correction: Run and record the focused product, cart, and checkout integration scenarios covering the listed combinations and HTTP status/order-creation assertions, then provide passing results for the exact reviewed head.

runs.report:
# Triage report

## Repository confirmation
The requested API paths and behavior belong to this Shopizer checkout. Relevant implementation is in `sm-shop`, `sm-core`, `sm-core-model`, and existing integration tests under `sm-shop/src/test`.

No linked GitHub issue or label catalog was supplied; no labels are suggested. Working tree is clean apart from the assigned checkout branch.

## Evidence

- Both API product DTOs already expose independent-looking `visible` and `available` fields: `sm-shop-model/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/model/catalog/product/Product.java:15-58`.
- The core product entity persists `AVAILABLE` but has no visibility field: `sm-core-model/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/core/model/catalog/product/Product.java:130-136`.
- The v1 write mapper currently assigns `source.isVisible()` to core availability, proving the reported coupling: `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/mapper/catalog/product/PersistableProductMapper.java:97-101`.
- The v2 definition write mapper has the same defect: `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/mapper/catalog/product/PersistableProductDefinitionMapper.java:72-80`.
- Read mappers expose availability but do not map a persisted visibility value: `ReadableProductMapper.java:120-122` and `ReadableProductDefinitionMapper.java:78-82`.
- Shopper list queries filter on `p.available`/`dateAvailable`, but not visibility: `sm-core/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/core/business/repositories/catalog/product/ProductRepositoryImpl.java:668-674` and `840-846`.
- v2 SKU lookup and friendly URL lookup retrieve products without a visibility check: `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/facade/product/ProductFacadeV2Impl.java:89-109` and `127-145`.
- The v1 facade similarly retrieves by SKU and friendly URL without a visibility check: `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/facade/product/ProductFacadeImpl.java:157-179` and `206-223`.
- The v1 API has a shopper `/api/v1/products` list but no `/api/v1/private/products` merchant list endpoint: `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/api/v1/product/ProductApi.java:185-212`.
- `/api/v1/private/**` is protected by `AUTH`: `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/application/config/MultipleEntryPointsSecurityConfig.java:327-336`.
- Cart add/update paths fetch products and reject unavailable products in `ShoppingCartFacadeImpl.java:180-320`; hidden-product rejection must be added separately from availability.
- Checkout loads the cart and delegates order creation without an explicit hidden-product guard: `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/api/v1/order/OrderApi.java:407-468`.
- Existing integration-test locations are `ProductManagementAPIIntegrationTest`, `ProductV2ManagementAPIIntegrationTest`, and `ShoppingCartAPIIntegrationTest`.

## Problem and scope

The product domain currently conflates visibility with availability. `visible` must become a separately persisted product property, while `available` must continue to represent purchasability. Shopper-facing reads, lists, add-to-cart, and checkout must enforce visibility; merchant product management must retain access to hidden products and return both flags.

Likely implementation scope:

1. Add a persisted visibility property to the core product entity and update the project’s schema/migration convention.
2. Correct v1 and v2 persistable mappers to map `available` from the request’s availability field and `visible` from the request’s visibility field.
3. Map both fields in all relevant readable product/definition/populator paths.
4. Apply `visible=true` to shopper list queries and ensure count/data queries use consistent predicates and correct boolean grouping.
5. Make shopper SKU and friendly-URL lookups return not-found for hidden products; ensure the friendly URL result matches SKU behavior.
6. Add the protected `/api/v1/private/products` merchant listing using the existing query parameters/response shape, with a merchant/admin origin that does not exclude hidden products and remains store-scoped.
7. Reject hidden products on cart add/update with HTTP 404, while retaining the existing unavailable-product behavior.
8. Validate cart contents immediately before checkout; hidden items must produce HTTP 409 and prevent order creation. Removing the item or setting visible true must allow checkout again.
9. Preserve order snapshots/line data so later visibility changes do not alter existing orders.

## Acceptance checks

- POST and PUT through `/api/v1/private/product` persist and read back all four combinations of `visible` and `available` independently.
- The equivalent v2 product-management flow remains consistent where applicable.
- A hidden product returns 404 from `/api/v2/product/{sku}` and `/api/v2/product/name/{friendlyUrl}`.
- Hidden products are absent from `/api/v1/products` and `/api/v2/products`, including pagination totals and filtered results.
- Hidden products cannot be added to a cart and receive HTTP 404.
- A cart containing a product hidden after insertion cannot be checked out; response is HTTP 409 and no order is created.
- Removing the hidden item, or showing it again, permits checkout.
- `/api/v1/private/products` requires the same private authentication boundary, is store-scoped, preserves the public list’s query parameters and response shape, includes hidden products, and returns `visible` accurately.
- Visible products return `visible=true` and the stored availability value. Visible but unavailable products return `available=false` and cannot be added to a cart.
- Re-showing a product restores shopper lookup/list/cart behavior without changing stock or price.
- Existing orders containing a product later hidden remain readable and unchanged.
- Existing product, cart, checkout, and API integration tests continue to pass.

## Likely affected components

- `sm-core-model`: product entity and persistence/schema mapping.
- `sm-shop-model`: product DTOs/readable definitions if a separate availability/visibility representation is needed.
- `sm-shop` product mappers, populators, facades, v1/v2 product APIs, and security-aware merchant listing.
- `sm-core` product repository criteria/query construction.
- `sm-shop` cart facade and order/checkout validation path.
- Product and cart integration tests, plus migration/database fixtures as required by repository conventions.

## Assumptions and risks

- Existing records should default to visible so current catalog behavior is preserved unless the repository migration convention specifies another default.
- Existing availability defaults should remain available unless explicitly sent otherwise.
- Visibility is product-level; variant availability remains separate unless tests demonstrate a required variant-specific rule.
- The requested HTTP statuses may require using the project’s existing `ResourceNotFoundException`, runtime exception/status mapping, and conflict handling rather than changing global error behavior.
- Checkout validation should occur before `processOrder` so a failed hidden-product check cannot create an order.

## Complexity

Medium-high. The root defect is straightforward, but the change requires a schema-level field, two write/read mapping families, shopper versus merchant query semantics, cart mutation and checkout safeguards, authentication/store scoping, and regression coverage across multiple integration APIs.

## Routing

This is sufficiently specified for direct Implement routing. No consequential design approval is required; implementation choices can follow the existing entity, mapper, repository, exception, security, and integration-test conventions.

Shopper listings/lookups exclude hidden products; merchants can use protected `/api/v1/private/products`; hidden products cannot enter carts; checkout returns 409 before order creation for carts containing newly hidden products. - git diff --check passed.

- Showing a hidden product again (replacing it with "visible": true) brings it back everywhere, with its stock and price unchanged. Orders that include a product that was hidden later are unaffected.

When you have finished, reply with one short paragraph saying what you changed.
</task>
